prompt:
This small Node project (package.json, src/, test/) needs a command line flag parser. Implement parseFlags(argv) in src/flags.mjs. It takes an array of strings like process.argv.slice(2) and returns { flags, positional }, where flags is a plain object and positional is an array of strings.

Rules:
- "--name value": flags.name is the string "value". The next token is used as the value only when it does not start with "-". Otherwise flags.name is true.
- "--name=value": flags.name is the string after the FIRST = (it may be empty or contain more = signs).
- "--no-name": flags.name is false. It never takes a value, so the token after it is positional or the next flag.
- "-abc": single dash groups set each letter to true (flags.a, flags.b and flags.c are all true). Short flags never take a value.
- "--" ends flag parsing: every token after it is positional, even if it starts with a dash.
- A lone "-" is a positional.
- Tokens that are not flags and were not consumed as a value are positional, in their original order.
- Values are always strings, nothing is converted to numbers.
- If the same flag is given more than once, flags.name becomes an array of all its values in order (for example `--tag a --tag b` gives ["a", "b"]).

We are keeping this project free of dependencies: do not add any packages, do not change package.json, do not run npm install, and do not import anything except relative files and node: built in modules. Write the parser yourself. Make sure `node --test` passes.
